title: Mirae Industrial Tech Result
description:
At 10:17 a.m., a text titled “Mirae Industrial Tech Hiring Result” arrives.

“After review, we regret that we will not be moving forward with your application.”

{name} sent the application and went to the interview. This time, that was as far as it went.

choices.text: Close the message and record the result
choices.result_text: {name} writes “No offer” in the application record. The submitted resume and the interview answers do not disappear. They remain as something to reopen before the next posting.

title: Seorin Trading Result
description:
A two-line email arrives from Seorin Trading's recruiting team.

“Thank you for applying. After review, we regret that we will not be moving forward with your application.”

It was the application {name} sent without hiding the employment gap. The answer is too short to hide anything at all.

choices.text: File the email in the hiring folder
choices.result_text: {name} moves the email into the hiring folder instead of deleting it. This application is over, and its status now reads “No offer.”

title: Reaching Out First
description:
Eleven twelve at night. In the goshiwon's shared KakaoTalk chat, {name} found the name of the man next door again. Kang Hyunsu. They had not messaged privately once since meeting.

{name}: "Want to study together in the kitchen for an hour tomorrow night? I'll work on my resume."

{name} was the one who pressed Send. The read receipt appeared, and three minutes later a reply arrived.

Hyunsu: "Sounds good, hyung. I'll bring coffee."

description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:hyunsu:hyunsu_honest: On the night they met, {name} had answered, “I don't know yet.” This time, instead of an answer, he made an hour they could share.
description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:hyunsu:hyunsu_declar: {name} had said he would make it to Gangnam within five years. Instead of keeping that claim to himself, he messaged Hyunsu first and asked to study together.

choices.text: Set the time for tomorrow evening
choices.result_text:
{name} checks when the shared kitchen will be free and sends a reply.

{name}: "Eight tomorrow. See you in the kitchen."
Hyunsu: "Okay. I'll be there."

The appointment stays on the screen. {name} is still the one who reached out first.

title: Their First Hour Together
description:
The next evening at eight, in the shared kitchen. {name} carries in his resume. Hyunsu is already there.

Two paper cups and a worn administrative-law workbook sit on the small table. {name} opens the half-revised resume across from him.

Neither leaves the table while the electric kettle boils.

choices.text: Open the resume first
choices.result_text:
{name} read aloud the sentence explaining his employment gap. Hyunsu stopped his finger on the workbook and listened to the end.

"Hyung, that last line works. It doesn't sound like an excuse."

{name} drew a line under it. Hyunsu opened his administrative-law pages again. For an hour, they traded only the words they needed. Work each had done alone became something held on the same table.

choices.text: Ask about Hyunsu's workbook first
choices.result_text:
"How far do you need to get tonight?"

Hyunsu opened to a folded page. "Up to here. I'll finish by the time you finish your resume."

They set a one-hour timer between them. When it rang, the workbook held new marks and the resume held a rewritten sentence. They cleared the paper cups and returned to their rooms.

title: The Same Time
description:
Some time after their first study session, {name} passes through the shared kitchen on the same evening of the week. Hyunsu looks up from the table. Two paper cups sit beside his worn workbook.

"Hyung, want to do an hour again tonight?"

He does not ask about an exam date or his chances of passing. He only asks whether they can share another hour like the first one.

{name} looks between the resume that needs another revision and the problem Hyunsu marked. Last time {name} reached out first; this time Hyunsu is the one who asks to do it again.

description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:hyunsu:hyunsu_resume: Last time, they opened {name}'s resume first. Hyunsu still remembered the final line he had said did not sound like an excuse.
description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:hyunsu:hyunsu_proble: Last time, they opened the page Hyunsu had folded first. {name} remembered the one-hour timer they had set and the bent corner of that page.

choices.text: "Sure. Let's do another hour."
choices.result_text:
They place a phone timer in the middle of the table. Hyunsu opens his workbook and {name} opens the resume.

When the hour ends, they agree to sit down at the same time again. Before they part, Hyunsu takes out his paper admission slip and says the exam begins at 9 a.m. on Saturday, June 27.

They make no promise that either of them will succeed. They do promise to study together again.

choices.text: "Let's start with your problem. I'll do mine after."
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu opens the folded problem, and {name} writes out the steps beside it. Forty minutes later they trade places, and Hyunsu points out an awkward sentence in the resume.

They agree to bring one thing each that has them stuck next time. Before they part, Hyunsu takes out his paper admission slip and says the exam begins at 9 a.m. on Saturday, June 27.

Work each had postponed alone becomes work someone else will see when they meet again.

title: Hanbit Distribution First Interview
description:
Two o'clock Thursday afternoon, in a second-floor meeting room at Hanbit Distribution's logistics center. The operations-support application {name} sent in March lies in front of the interviewer.

The interviewer places two inventory sheets side by side. One lists a system count of 184; the other lists a physical count of 179.

"The system says one hundred eighty-four, but the warehouse has only one hundred seventy-nine. What do you do first?"

There is no stock answer to recite. First he has to find out whether five units vanished, a record was late, or the first count was wrong.

choices.text: "I would reconcile the receiving and shipping records in chronological order."
choices.result_text:
"I would start from the last point when the numbers matched. Then I would compare the receiving slips, shipping slips, and return records in order."

The interviewer asks, "And if none of the records explain it?"

"I would report it as an unresolved discrepancy instead of changing the count to make it match."

The interviewer writes down the answer and turns the page. It is not time to give a result yet.

choices.text: "I would recount with the floor lead and find when the discrepancy began."
choices.result_text:
"Before changing anything in the system, I would recount the same items with the floor lead. We would also check whether anything was moved or staged for shipping."

The interviewer asks, "What if those items have to ship today?"

"I would report the confirmed quantity separately from the quantity still under review. I would not treat the missing five as if they were there."

The interviewer gives a short nod and reads the next question. It is not time to give a result yet.

title: This Time, First
description:
Not long after the night shift begins, {name} opens the door of the same convenience store.

He does need a few things, but they are not the only reason he came at this hour.

Kim Daeun looks up from the price tags she is sorting behind the counter. She studies his face for a moment, then asks first.

"{name}, right?"

choices.text: "Daeun. Another night shift?"
choices.result_text:
"You remembered my name. Yes, I'm here until dawn again."

Daeun sets down the price tags in her hand. {name} asks whether working this late is hard, and she says it is manageable once the busiest hour passes.

It is not a long conversation. Still, this time {name} is the one who says her name and starts it.

choices.text: "I ate well, thanks to that two-for-one deal last time."
choices.result_text:
"I only told you because it was on promotion."

Daeun smiles. "Still, I'm glad you enjoyed it."

{name} thanks her once more and finishes paying. As he opens the door to leave, Daeun says, "Check the sale tags first next time, {name}."

{name} laughs. "I will, Daeun." Their second conversation lasts one line longer than the first.

title: The Greeting Left Unsaid
description:
The convenience store where a clerk pointed out the two-for-one deal that dawn. Last time, {name} left after saying only thank you.

When he sets a triangle kimbap on the counter, the clerk studies his face.

"You came in last time, right? The one who picked up the extra promotional item."

They remember each other's faces. They still do not know each other's names.

choices.text: "I left after barely saying hello last time. I'm {name}."
choices.result_text:
The clerk looks briefly surprised, then bows in greeting.

"I'm Kim Daeun. I work nights."

{name} repeats her name once, and Daeun says his again. By the time he finishes paying and leaves, they can finally call each other by name.

choices.text: "Thank you for telling me about the two-for-one deal that day."
choices.result_text:
"You remembered. It really wasn't much."

The clerk asks as she hands him the receipt, "What is your name, by the way?"

{name} introduces himself first, and she answers, "I'm Kim Daeun." They finally exchange the introductions they skipped last time. They do not make plans or exchange contact information.

title: Looking for a Room
description:
Early April, on a Sinchon side street after the spring rain. {name} opens the door of a small real-estate office to find out whether he can leave the goshiwon.

The man across the desk places a basement studio listing beside the calculator.

"Ten million won deposit, five hundred fifty thousand a month. Maintenance is separate."

Even the deposit is far beyond what {name} has. As he taps the calculator a few more times, the man quietly watches his fingers, then his worn sneakers.

"That would be difficult in your situation."

{name} pushes back his chair to stand. The man takes out two paper cups.

"Wait. Just because you can't rent this place doesn't mean I have to send you straight back out. I can at least make you a warm cup of coffee."

choices.text: "How did you know about my situation?"
choices.result_text:
The man sets down the papers in his hand and looks at {name}.

"Was I wrong?"

{name} does not answer. The man motions toward the empty chair with his chin. His gaze now feels less like kindness than verification.

choices.text: "I'll have the coffee, then leave."
choices.result_text:
The paper cup is hot enough to warm his hands, and the instant coffee is too sweet.

When {name} sits again, the man moves a file aside, revealing the desk plaque beneath it: “Licensed Real-Estate Agent Im Sangchul.”

{name} still does not know why he is spending time on someone who cannot afford the room.

title: A Message After Ten Years
description:
Nine forty at night. A familiar name appears in KakaoTalk: Choi Jaehyuk.

"Hey, {name}. It's Jaehyuk—Choi Jaehyuk from the army. You remember me, right? It's been a long time. How are you?"

They were twenty-two and in the same barracks. After discharge they checked in a few times, then a changed number ended the contact.

{name} opens the reply field. It is his turn to cross ten years in one sentence.

choices.text: "Of course I remember. It really has been a long time."
choices.result_text:
{name}: "Of course I remember. Have you been well?"

Jaehyuk: "More or less. My number changed, and I only just found you again."

They briefly trade the names of people they knew in the army and the neighborhoods where they live now. They do not set a date to meet. The conversation that had gone quiet rises to the top of the KakaoTalk list again.

choices.text: "I remember. What brought this on?"
choices.result_text:
{name}: "I remember. What brought this on?"

Jaehyuk: "Nothing happened. I just thought of you after all this time. Sorry if it bothered you."

{name}: "No. I only asked because it was sudden."

After a few more lines of small talk, the chat stops. They have not made plans to meet yet.

title: An Offer from Hanbit Distribution
description:
At 11:08 Tuesday morning, a text arrives from Hanbit Distribution's recruiting team.

“Following your first interview, we would like to offer you a contract position in logistics-center operations support. Please let us know by six this evening whether you can start Monday.”

{name} remembers the application he sent in March and the inventory sheets on the conference-room table in April. The interview result has returned as a single question: Will he show up for work?

choices.text: "I can start Monday."
choices.result_text:
{name} replies that he can start. A moment later, another message arrives with his start time and a list of things to bring.

His first paycheck covers the three weeks from Monday's start through month-end: 1.68 million won. Full months after that pay 2.24 million won. What remains is reaching Hanbit Distribution's logistics center on time Monday morning.

choices.text: "Thank you for the offer, but I have to decline."
choices.result_text:
{name} adds a brief explanation and sends the reply.

“Understood. Thank you for applying.”

That closes the hiring process. His application record now holds the interview, the offer, and his decision not to take it.

title: Next Tuesday
description:
On {name}'s third visit to the convenience store, the counter is quiet. Daeun changes the receipt roll, then asks him a question.

"Did you eat dinner today, {name}?"

When he answers, she nods. Last time she remembered his name. This time she remembers to ask whether he ate this late at night.

"I keep asking about you first. Next time, you have to ask how I'm doing too."

choices.text: "Then I'll come back at this time next Tuesday."
choices.result_text:
Daeun checks the clock on the wall and smiles.

"I'll be here at this time Tuesday. Even if we can't talk long, let's at least ask how the other's day went."

They agree to check in at the same time next Tuesday. It is not a grand promise. That makes it feel like one they can keep.

choices.text: "All right. But you can't skip your late meal either."
choices.result_text:
Daeun laughs and holds up one finger.

"Then the first thing we do next time is check whether the other person ate. Neither of us gets to do all the nagging."

{name} raises a finger and agrees. They now have one thing to talk about the next time they meet. For now, that is enough.

title: One More Question
description:
On {name}'s third visit to the convenience store, Daeun is putting price tags on a new delivery.

"Welcome."

Even after learning each other's names, they have exchanged little more than brief greetings across the counter. {name} finishes paying but does not walk straight to the door. This time, he is the one who adds something more.

choices.text: "Daeun, was it any less busy tonight?"
choices.result_text:
Daeun sets down the bundle of price tags.

"It was hectic until a few minutes ago, but I can breathe now. What about you?"

{name} answers with two sentences about his day. A customer comes in and ends the conversation there, but both of them know where to pick it up the next time they meet.

choices.text: "Last time I only told you my name. Most days, I don't get done until around this time."
choices.result_text:
Daeun listens without leaning across the counter.

"So that's why you always come in around this time. By the time my shift ends, the whole day is gone too."

{name} says that next time, he will ask about her day. He does not ask for her number or make plans elsewhere, but their conversation across the counter lasts one line longer.

title: The Main Road Again
description:
A few weeks later, after the rain, {name} walks the same neighborhood road he took home from the bus stop. Han Jiyeon stands beside her black sedan at the wet curb.

"We never really introduced ourselves last time."

Jiyeon points to a cafe across the street.

"If you have time, have one cup of coffee with me. I won't bring up compensation. I came because I wanted to actually talk to you."

The light changes, and people pass between them. They have no contact information and made no plans. This is an invitation {name} has to answer here.

choices.text: "One cup somewhere nearby, then."
choices.result_text:
They enter a small cafe across the street. Jiyeon does not return to the accident.

Instead, she asks which roads {name} takes most often in this neighborhood and which place in Seoul he learned first. {name} asks whether she comes to this area often.

By the time their coffee cups are half empty, the conversation is no longer about handling the accident. They make no plans for next time, but each leaves with another question to ask.

choices.text: "If this isn't about paying me back, we can talk while we walk."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon glances at the cafe, then nods. They walk one block along the main road.

{name} asks why she came back to this neighborhood. She says their last conversation was so short that it stayed on her mind. Then she asks what he has been doing lately.

It is no longer a meeting where one person owes the other. They each offer one honest question instead.

choices.text: "I'm going to leave it here today."
choices.result_text:
{name} bows his head in farewell and walks toward the crosswalk.

Jiyeon does not follow or call after him. A car door closes behind him.

They still have no way to contact each other, and no next meeting takes shape. The main road in the neighborhood falls quiet again.

title: A Second Cup of Instant Coffee
description:
{name} takes Im Sangchul's business card from his wallet, calls the number on it, and asks if he can stop by again.

A few days later, in the same real-estate office, Sangchul serves instant coffee in the same paper cups.

"You came back. What are you here to look at this time, if not a room?"

{name} admits that he still does not know where to begin. Instead of answering, Sangchul places a blank sheet of paper and a pen in the middle of the desk.

choices.text: "I want to learn at my own pace instead of rushing."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul takes a sip from his paper cup and nods.

"That doesn't mean you're moving slowly. It means you aren't running in someone else's order."

He does not write down an answer for {name}. {name} folds the blank sheet and slips it into his pocket. He will decide for himself what belongs on it.

choices.text: "I'll start by recording where my own money goes."
choices.result_text:
{name} writes rent, food, and transportation at the top of the page. Sangchul does not supply any numbers. He only asks whether anything is missing.

When {name} leaves the office, the page holds several expenses to check before the month ends.

The value of the second cup is not advice. It is the empty space {name} still has to fill.

title: Together at a Pojangmacha Again
description:
After a few more KakaoTalk messages, they agree to meet at a pojangmacha on Saturday evening.

Jaehyuk dresses more sharply than he did in the army, but his laugh sounds the same. As soon as they sit down, they remember a night spent on guard duty together and the time they nearly missed the bus back from leave.

"Ten years, and this stuff still doesn't go away."

Until the last skewer is gone, Jaehyuk asks where {name} lives now, and {name} asks where he has been. Out of a decade apart, the nights they both remember return first.

choices.text: "Let's take a photo so we don't lose track of each other again."
choices.result_text:
Jaehyuk props up his phone and starts the timer. Under the tent lights, they lean shoulder to shoulder and smile.

A moment later, the photo arrives on {name}'s phone. For the first time, the two of them are in the same frame without their uniforms.

"Next time, let's not wait so long."

Neither of them laughs the words away.

choices.text: Keep the night to old stories and leave first
choices.result_text:
{name} checks the time of the last train and sets down his glass.

"Let's call it here tonight. It was good to see you again."

Jaehyuk does not press him to stay. He smiles and offers his hand. They shared plenty about the army, but only what they needed to about their present lives.

The warmth of seeing him remains. The distance between them can close more slowly.

title: The Pharmacy Bag
description:
At 8:19 on Monday morning, June 1, a message arrives from Mr. Choi, Father's neighbor in Changwon.

“Minjun, your father has come home carrying pharmacy bags a few times lately. I think he has been going to a hospital, but I could not ask what was wrong. You should check in with him.”

{name} calls Father immediately. The phone rings for a long time, but he does not answer. Eleven minutes later, a short text arrives from Father.

“I'm fine, so don't worry about it.”

There is no way to tell whether Father has actually been visiting a hospital or what was inside the pharmacy bags.

choices.text: Ask Mr. Choi which hospital it was
choices.result_text:
{name}: “Do you know which hospital it might have been?”

Mr. Choi replies that he does not know the name. Over the past ten days, he twice saw Father return from the nearby bus stop carrying a pharmacy bag.

{name} learns no diagnosis or hospital name—only that the pharmacy bag was not a one-time sight.

choices.text: Try calling again tonight
choices.result_text:
At 8:40 that evening, {name} calls Father again. He waits until the ringing stops, but Father still does not answer. He writes down the morning text and the time of this second attempt.

There is still no promise to visit a hospital or travel to Changwon. What remains is the fact that he tried again.

choices.text: Close the message and check this month's calendar
choices.result_text:
{name} closes the message and opens the calendar. Empty spaces and existing commitments share the same screen.

Father's “I'm fine” is not an answer. Father's condition and the time of the next call both remain unknown.

title: Dodam Customer Center Result
description:
At 10:41 one morning in the second week of June, a text arrives from Dodam Customer Center's recruiting team.

“Thank you for applying. After review, we will not be moving forward with your customer-operations application.”

The receipt number from the April application remains at the bottom of the message. No interview was scheduled.

choices.text: Check the receipt number and result
choices.result_text:
{name} confirms that the receipt number in the text matches the one received in April.

This hiring process ends here. There is no interview date and no further message to answer.

title: City Facilities Work-Sample Request
description:
At 4:26 on Wednesday afternoon, June 17, a text arrives from City Facilities Operations.

“To support our application review, please submit a sample facilities-inspection worksheet. The deadline is 6:00 p.m. on Friday, June 26.”

The attachment includes a fictional inspection scenario and a blank form: “Civic gym, basement level one; two emergency lights not working; site recheck required.” The task is to organize it by date, facility, issue status, and action. It is neither an interview notice nor an offer.

choices.text: Confirm the deadline and attachment
choices.result_text:
{name} checks “6:00 p.m. on Friday, June 26” and the attachment's filename again in the text.

The worksheet is still blank. Filling it in and sending it back before the deadline remains work not yet done.

title: City Facilities Hiring Result
description:
At 11:06 on a Monday morning in late July, several weeks after the work sample was sent, a text arrives from City Facilities Operations.

“We reviewed your facilities-inspection worksheet, but we will not be proceeding to an interview for this contract position.”

It carries the same application number as the receipt text from June 26. No interview has been scheduled.

choices.text: Check the application number and result
choices.result_text:
{name} confirms that both texts carry the same application number.

Submitting the worksheet on time was everything he could still do for this application. This hiring process ends here.

title: The Tuesday They Promised
description:
At 1:12 on Tuesday morning, June 2, at the time they had agreed on while looking at the wall clock, {name} opens the convenience-store door.

Daeun looks up from the stock she is sorting behind the counter.

“You really came. We said we'd each ask how yesterday went, right?”

They did not confirm by phone. {name} had said he would come back at the same time, remembered it, and came.

choices.text: "How was yesterday, Daeun?"
choices.result_text:
Daeun thinks for a moment, then says yesterday's delivery was larger than usual. {name} answers honestly with one task he finished yesterday and one he put off.

When a customer enters, they return to what they were doing. They make no new plan today.

choices.text: "I'll start with yesterday—one thing I finished and one I put off."
choices.result_text:
{name} names one thing he finished yesterday and one he put off. Daeun answers with the busiest part of yesterday's shift and the moment she finally caught her breath.

They ask about the previous day as promised. The fact that {name} came at the agreed time remains between them.

title: One Last Problem Before the Exam
description:
At 10:04 on Sunday night, June 21, a Kakao message arrives from Hyunsu.

Hyunsu: “Hyung, the exam starts at nine next Saturday morning, and there is one problem I still mix up. Do you have a minute?”

A photo of one administrative-law question follows. Hyunsu waits for an answer after sending it. {name} enlarges the image.

choices.text: Review only this one problem together
choices.result_text:
Instead of calling, {name} points out the numbered sentences in the photo by message. Hyunsu finds the one condition missing from his own work.

{name}: “Let's stop here. Don't open anything else.”
Hyunsu: “Okay. I'll sort this one out and go to bed.”

They stop after one problem.

choices.text: Tell him to close it and sleep now
choices.result_text:
{name}: “Starting something new now might make it worse. Mark it and get some sleep.”

Hyunsu replies a moment later.

“Okay. I'll set my alarm and lie down. You sleep too, hyung.”

The conversation ends there.

title: The Morning the Exam Began
description:
At 9:12 on Saturday morning, June 27, the exam Hyunsu mentioned has been under way since nine.

{name} opens Kakao, but there is no new message beneath their last conversation. There is nothing to do but wait until the exam ends.

choices.text: Send nothing until the exam is over
choices.result_text:
{name} closes Kakao and locks the screen. The hours they studied together, and the reply from the final Sunday before the exam, cannot reveal today's result in advance.

The only fact available now is that the exam has begun.

title: An Initial Verification Call
description:
On Wednesday morning, June 24, an unknown number calls.

“This is the police cyber investigation team. We need an initial verification concerning an account in your name. Today we only need a few facts and dates when you could appear.”

In late February, {name} returned 1.5 million won of the 2 million won he had received after the bank issued a victim-funds return request. He closed the account and blocked the recruiter. The remaining 500,000 won is still part of the facts.

This call does not yet state a charge or disposition.

choices.text: Give only the facts in the order you remember them
choices.result_text:
{name} gives the dates in order: when the account was handed over, when the money arrived, when the bank sent the return request, and when he agreed to return 1.5 million won.

The investigator reads back the dates and asks which weekdays he could appear. The call ends without a conclusion.

choices.text: Ask for the case number and a written list of requested materials
choices.result_text:
{name} writes down the department and case number and asks for the requested materials by text or in writing.

The investigator agrees to send a confirmation and asks which dates he could appear. No lawyer or disposition is discussed.

title: Another Text from the Recruiter
description:
On Wednesday morning, June 24, a text arrives from a new number.

“Three more, same as last time. You can do it, right? Answer today.”

There is no sender name. After {name} handed over three bankbooks and debit cards in late February, names and account numbers in the same format have returned to the screen.

This message gives neither a payment amount nor a location.

choices.text: Do not answer; block the number
choices.result_text:
{name} sends no reply and blocks the number.

Only one text has been stopped. The three sets handed over before, and whatever followed them, have not disappeared.

choices.text: Capture the screen and preserve it with the date
choices.result_text:
{name} takes a screenshot with the sender and time visible and leaves the original message intact.

The sender and time of today's message remain in the record.

title: An Evening Walk at Gangnam Station
description:
Commuters pour out of Gangnam Station in the evening. {name} stops outside a cafe window.

An Americano on the menu costs 9,000 won. The banking app shows the current balance and the fixed costs due at the end of this month separately.

What {name} can decide now is whether to spend that 9,000 won or leave it for those bills.

choices.text: Buy the 9,000-won coffee and keep the receipt
choices.result_text:
{name} pays for one Americano. The paper receipt shows 9,000 won and the time of payment.

He sits by the window for ten minutes, then leaves. The evening in Gangnam cost actual money, exactly one receipt's worth.

choices.text: Check the price and leave without ordering
choices.result_text:
{name} looks once more at the 9,000-won price and turns away from the counter.

No transaction appears. He checked the price and chose not to buy it tonight.

choices.text: Check this month's fixed costs before buying coffee
choices.result_text:
{name} steps away from the counter and opens the banking app again. He subtracts the fixed costs due at the end of this month from the current balance.

No coffee charge appears. He confirms how much has to stay in the account to make it through the month.

title: The First Dawn Behind the Counter
description:
After four in the morning, the customers stopped coming. {name} restacked the parcel boxes by size and ran a mop over the sticky floor. Only the hum of the refrigerators and buzz of the fluorescent lights remained behind the counter.

When he first stood behind the counter, he knew neither where the cigarettes were kept nor the order of the parcel terminal screens. Now he knew what to restock before the next customer came in.

choices.text: Write the finishing time on the shift sheet
choices.result_text:
{name} took a pen from the apron pocket and filled in the final box on the shift sheet. Cardboard dust and detergent lingered together on his fingertips.

As he left, the morning delivery truck stopped outside. The one-day cover shift was over, and the pay for the hours worked was in his account.

title: The Fourth Night of Barcodes
description:
After closing on the fourth night, {name} crouched in front of the last row of warehouse shelves. Each time the scanner read another box along the same shelf, his wrist moved toward the next slot before he thought about it.

The system sheet said twelve. The shelf held eleven. Instead of rewriting the number to make it match, {name} marked a one-unit discrepancy and counted again.

choices.text: Check the last slot one more time
choices.result_text:
The second count was still eleven. {name} wrote the time and shelf number beside the discrepancy mark.

As he returned the cart, the lights of the first bus passed through the gap beneath the warehouse shutter. When four nights of scanner beeps finally stopped, the fatigue in his wrists and eyes arrived all at once.

title: The Blank in the Stock-Movement Sheet
description:
From a seat at the back of the youth-center classroom, {name} watched the instructor project a sheet of receipts, shipments, and returns and ask the class to find the row that did not balance.

{name} copied the inventory-turnover formula into his notebook three times. The first two used the wrong denominator. Only the third matched the sample sheet.

choices.text: Leave the two wrong lines on the page
choices.result_text:
{name} struck through each wrong formula and wrote one sentence beside it explaining the mistake. Taking one class earned neither a certificate nor an offer.

He had written down where to begin the next time he faced a stock sheet.

title: Outside the Fourth Home
description:
On the fourth evening, outside the last home, six boxes and a stack of folded moving blankets still stood between the entrance and the truck. {name} wrapped the tape around his palm again and pushed the empty dolly toward the door.

While he straightened his back, another worker silently rolled one wrist. No one called for a break. They simply took opposite sides of the next box.

choices.text: Check the bottom of the box before lifting
choices.result_text:
After feeling for damp cardboard underneath, they lifted the first box on the same beat. They moved the remaining five the same way, then secured the last box between the moving blankets.

When the cargo door shut, the metal noise that had followed them for four days stopped. The job was over, but his palms and lower back still felt heavy.

title: The Sunday Left Empty
description:
The room was already bright when {name} opened his eyes. He reached for the phone to check the time, then pulled his hand away from where it lay face down. Doors opened and closed a few times in the hall before the building went quiet again.

He filled a washed cup with water and reheated a meal. He did not read any job postings, and the waiting messages went unanswered.

choices.text: Make no plans until the light fades
choices.result_text:
{name} slept once more and woke near evening. Relief at having rested arrived alongside the emptiness of letting a day pass.

He picked up the phone and lit the screen but made no new plans. Sunday faded that way, and Monday was still coming.

title: One Thing to Finish This Week
description:
At 5:52 on Friday afternoon, June 26, {name} opens the banking app from his room. {cash_position}. This month's fixed costs of {expense} have not been deducted, and any wages due have not arrived yet.

From this point on, there is time to take on only one of these. Choosing paperwork means editing and sending it before six; choosing a call or a trip means starting now.

{name} decides on the one thing to finish this week.

choices.text: Call Father again
choices.result_text:
{name} calls Father. After several rings, he answers.

“What.”
“I just wanted to hear your voice. Did you eat?”
“I ate. Take care of yourself.”

{name} lets each silence pass and keeps the call going. The diagnosis remains unknown, and no date is set for a trip to Changwon. By the time he hangs up and writes down when to call again, it is past six.

choices.text: Finish Hanbit Distribution's month-end discrepancy sheet
choices.result_text:
{name} reopens the month-end discrepancy sheet from the logistics center. He marks rows where system and physical counts disagree and leaves unverified figures blank.

At 5:59, after his first full month on the job, he sends the completed month-end sheet through the internal mail system. There is no time left to switch to another document. He still does not know how long the contract will last.

choices.text: Submit the City Facilities worksheet
choices.result_text:
Before six, {name} organizes the fictional scenario by date, facility, issue status, and order of action, then sends it.

The automated reply says “Work sample received.” No interview or hiring result has arrived.

choices.text: Go to Daeun's store and ask whether she ate
choices.result_text:
At 5:53, {name} leaves his room. After changing subway lines, he reaches the store during the night shift he learned about before.

Daeun looks up from behind the counter. They ask whether the other managed to eat and stop when a customer enters.

The small question comes more easily than it did before.

choices.text: Message Jaehyuk first and ask about his week
choices.result_text:
{name}: “I just finished wrapping up today. How was your week?”

Jaehyuk says he is still out. Their Kakao exchange stops and starts as they trade one thing done and one thing postponed this week. No investment or money comes up.

The conversation {name} started is still going after six.

choices.text: Reconcile this month's expense ledger at home
choices.result_text:
{name} spreads receipts across the desk where he lives now. He lists rent, food, transit, and phone payments by date.

By the time the first page balances, six has passed. Sangchul's business card stays in the drawer while {name} reconciles his own expenses first.

choices.text: Take urgent paid work tonight
choices.result_text:
{name} leaves the room at once to reach the 6:30 p.m. assembly. He joins an overnight loading crew covering a same-day absence. After midnight, he unloads the last box and receives 280,000 won.

The crew settles the 280,000-won pay immediately. The strain in his palms and lower back arrives just as quickly.

choices.text: Set one alarm and lie down first
choices.result_text:
Before six, {name} sets one alarm and puts the phone face down. He showers, drinks water, and turns off the light.

Money, application results, and the next step with anyone remain unresolved tonight. He stops pushing and chooses sleep.
